script: This pigeon is more famous than the battle it supposedly saved. In October 1918, 500 American soldiers got trapped in France - shelled by their own army. Major Whittlesey sent his last pigeon, Cher Ami, through gunfire with one message: stop the barrage. Wounded, it still made the 25 miles in 25 minutes. Here's the twist: one report says the shelling had already stopped before that message arrived. The real story isn't the rescue - it's the flight itself.

metadata.title: Random But True: Cher Ami, the Pigeon Whose Rescue Is a Myth
metadata.caption:
Cher Ami flew 25 miles through WWI gunfire to deliver one message: stop the friendly-fire barrage hitting 500 trapped American soldiers.

The bird made it. Badly wounded, but it made it.

Here's the part the legend skips: a 1928 report on the incident found the shelling had already stopped by the time that message was actually received.

The pigeon didn't need to save the battle to be worth remembering - flying through it wounded was already the remarkable part.

Comment if you'd heard the "saved the battalion" version before today.
